note: new feature axis: channel_hist_log_vpd - a channel's own historical performance (mean log(views/day) of its OTHER videos in the dataset), looked up by channel_id. Split-aware and leak-safe: stats computed from split == 'train' only, with leave-one-out for train rows themselves (see train.py's _add_channel_history_feature); NaN (imputed) for channels with no other train-split video, which is most channels (only 1153/4241 channels have 2+ videos - covers 4745/7837 rows). channel_id was backfilled for the existing 7837-row cache via the YouTube Data API (videos.list, part=snippet) and is now captured going forward by both scrape.py and api_scrape.py. Re-froze benchmark/dataset.csv to bring the new column in, but row count and train/val/test split are unchanged (5449/1216/1172, same video_id hashes) - directly comparable to gen-6, not a new epoch. log_r2 0.675 -> 0.699, log_mse 1.645 -> 1.522, mdape 69.0% -> 65.7%.
